title: Vasquez Rocks Natural Area (Frankenstein 1931)
description: The tilted sandstone slabs here stood in for the mountains above Frankenstein's village, where Henry separates from the search party and is cornered by the Monster. The park is open daily as the Vasquez Rocks Natural Area and Nature Center in Agua Dulce.

title: Malibou Lake (Frankenstein 1931)
description: The lakeside where the Monster meets little Maria and drowns her was shot at Malibou Lake in the Santa Monica Mountains. The lake itself sits inside a gated private community, so it can only be glimpsed from Mulholland Highway.

title: Little Europe backlot street, Universal Studios Hollywood (Frankenstein 1931)
description: Most of the village exteriors for Frankenstein and Bride of Frankenstein were shot on Universal's European village sets. The sets standing today are a 1967 rebuild after a fire destroyed the originals, and they are seen from the Studio Tour tram rather than on foot.

title: Red Rock Canyon State Park (The Mummy 1932)
description: The Mojave badlands here doubled for Egypt in the tomb excavation scenes and the ancient Egyptian flashback. The park is a California state park with a visitor center and marked trails.

title: Former RKO Studios, Gower Street (Cat People 1942)
description: Val Lewton's Cat People was made entirely on RKO's Gower Street stages, partly on sets left over from The Magnificent Ambersons. The old RKO lot is now the eastern half of Paramount Pictures, and the Gower Street gate is still in use.

title: Former MGM lot, Culver City (Freaks 1932)
description: Tod Browning shot Freaks in 36 days on MGM's Culver City lot, reusing standing sets from a Garbo picture. The lot survives as a working studio in Culver City and is not open to the public, so it can only be seen from Washington Boulevard.

title: Psycho house, Universal backlot (Psycho 1960)
description: The Bates house was built on the Universal backlot in 1960 as a two sided facade, with the rear and right side added in 1964 for the new Studio Tour. It still stands and is one of the stops on the Universal Studios Hollywood backlot tram tour.

title: Bates Motel set, Universal backlot (Psycho 1960)
description: The twelve unit motel below the house was a backlot exterior, with the office and cabin interiors shot on Stage 18. The set has been rebuilt more than once and is still part of the Universal Studios Hollywood backlot tour.

title: Barrister Place, former Jefferson Hotel, Phoenix (Psycho 1960)
description: The hotel room where Marion and Sam meet on her lunch hour was the Jefferson Hotel at Central Avenue and Jefferson Street. The building survives as Barrister Place, having served as the Phoenix Police Museum from 1990 to 2014 before being sold to private developers.

title: 4270 Lankershim Boulevard, Los Angeles (Psycho 1960)
description: Marion trades her car at California Charlie's, filmed at what was then Harry Maher's used car lot on Lankershim Boulevard. The site is still a car dealership today.

title: Piazza C.L.N., Turin (Deep Red 1975)
description: This Fascist era square with its twin river fountains is where Marc lives and where he witnesses the killing of the psychic Helga. The Blue Bar was a set built in the square for the film, modelled on Hopper's Nighthawks, and it no longer exists.

title: Villa Scott, Turin (Deep Red 1975)
description: Pietro Fenoglio's Art Nouveau villa on Corso Giovanni Lanza played the Villa of the Screaming Child, the setting for the film's climax. It is privately owned and can only be looked at from the street, so view it from the sidewalk and do not approach the gate.

title: Teatro Carignano, Turin (Deep Red 1975)
description: Helga Ulmann's parapsychology lecture, the scene where she senses the killer in the audience, was staged in Turin's oldest theatre. The Carignano is still a working playhouse and runs behind the scenes tours.

title: Galleria San Federico, Turin (Deep Red 1975)
description: Marc and Carlo walk and talk through this 1933 shopping arcade, which also housed the offices of the La Stampa newspaper. The gallery and its cinema are still open to the public.

title: Mausoleum of Santa Costanza, Rome (Deep Red 1975)
description: Marc rehearses with his ensemble inside this fourth century circular mausoleum on the Via Nomentana. It is open to visitors and its original ceiling mosaics survive.

title: Museo delle Arti e Tradizioni Popolari, Rome (Deep Red 1975)
description: The folklore library where Marc digs into the legend of the haunted house is this ethnographic museum in Mussolini's EUR district. It is now part of the Museo delle Civilta and is open to the public.

title: Teatro Regio di Parma (Opera 1987)
description: Argento staged his cursed production of Verdi's Macbeth in Parma's neoclassical opera house, including the shots of Betty forced to watch murders with pins taped under her eyelids. The Teatro Regio is still one of Italy's major opera houses and runs guided tours.

title: Museum Rietberg, Zurich (Phenomena 1985)
description: The Villa Wesendonck in the Rietberg museum park served as the exterior of the Richard Wagner Academy for girls. The museum is open to visitors and the park is free to walk through.

title: Urnasch, Appenzell Ausserrhoden (Phenomena 1985)
description: The opening sequence, in which a young tourist misses the bus on a lonely country road and stumbles into the killer's house, was shot on the lanes around Urnasch. The village is a working Appenzell farming community reachable by the Appenzeller Bahnen railway.

title: Thur waterfalls, Alt St. Johann (Phenomena 1985)
description: One of the murders plays out at the Thur waterfalls in the Toggenburg valley below the Churfirsten peaks. The falls are on a marked public hiking route between Unterwasser and Alt St. Johann.

title: Gapstow Bridge, Central Park (Inferno 1980)
description: Kazanian drowns a sack of cats in the pond beside Gapstow Bridge, then falls in among the rats himself. The stone bridge at the north end of the Pond is one of Central Park's most photographed spots and is open to walk across.

title: Biblioteca Angelica, Rome (Inferno 1980)
description: The library interiors, where Mark's friend Sara finds the book of The Three Mothers and is followed into the cellars, were shot in this seventeenth century library near Piazza Navona. The Angelica is a working public library and its reading room can be visited.

title: Piazza Mincio, Quartiere Coppede, Rome (Inferno 1980)
description: The exterior entrance used for the library sits in the Coppede quarter, a small pocket of 1920s fantasy architecture around the Fountain of the Frogs. The square is a public street and free to wander.

title: Castello Massimo, Arsoli (Black Sunday 1960)
description: Prince Massimo's castle in the hill town of Arsoli east of Rome provided the exterior of the Vajda castle where Princess Asa returns from the grave. The castle is still owned by the Massimo family and opens for limited guided visits.

title: Orto Botanico di Roma (Black Sunday 1960)
description: The garden fountain scene between Princess Katia and her father was filmed in Rome's botanical garden on the slope of the Janiculum. The garden belongs to Sapienza University and is open to the public for an entrance fee.

title: TWA Flight Center, JFK Airport (Zombi 2 1979)
description: The airport lounge scenes were shot inside Eero Saarinen's 1962 TWA terminal at Kennedy Airport. The building sat empty for years and reopened in 2019 as the TWA Hotel, so the swooping lobby can now be walked through.

title: Fairview-Riverside State Park, Madisonville (The Beyond 1981)
description: The Victorian Otis House inside this Louisiana state park was the Seven Doors Hotel, the building sitting on one of the gateways to hell. The park is open to visitors and the house can be toured, with the hotel interiors having been built on a Rome sound stage.

title: 1221 Orange Street, New Orleans (The Beyond 1981)
description: The house where the blind girl Emily lives with her dog Dickie is a real home in the Lower Garden District. This is a private residence, so look at it from the sidewalk and do not knock.

title: Dillard University, New Orleans (The Beyond 1981)
description: The white colonnaded buildings of this historically Black university stood in for the hospital where Dr McCabe works. Dillard is an active campus, so visitors should stay on the public walkways.

title: Cornstalk Hotel, New Orleans (The Beyond 1981)
description: The hotel and its famous cast iron cornstalk fence appear behind Liza and McCabe as they walk through the French Quarter to the bookshop. It is still a working hotel on Royal Street and the fence is visible from the pavement.

title: Bonaventure Cemetery, Savannah (City of the Living Dead 1980)
description: Savannah played the cursed town of Dunwich, and this riverside cemetery is where Father Thomas hangs himself and where the survivors dig into his tomb. Bonaventure is a city cemetery open to visitors daily.

title: East River Street, Savannah (City of the Living Dead 1980)
description: The cobbled lane, iron pedestrian bridges and long stone stairs behind the River Street warehouses are where the boy is chased by the ghost zombies. The whole stretch is a public waterfront street lined with shops and bars.

title: The Ellis House, Scituate (The House by the Cemetery 1981)
description: This shingled house on Country Way was the exterior of the Freudstein place, with the tomb filled interiors built at a studio in Rome. It is private property used as an art studio, so view it from the road and do not enter the grounds.

title: Leticia, Amazonas (Cannibal Holocaust 1980)
description: Deodato based the Amazon shoot in and around this Colombian river town on the Amazon, chosen after a Colombian documentary maker recommended it. Leticia is a working port city reachable by air or riverboat.

title: Empire State Building, New York (Cannibal Holocaust 1980)
description: The New York framing scenes, including the skyline that opens the film, were shot in Manhattan with the Empire State Building among the locations used. The observation decks are open to ticket holders.

title: Monasterio de Santa Maria la Real de Valdeiglesias (Tombs of the Blind Dead 1972)
description: The roofless Cistercian ruins at Pelayos de la Presa are the abbey where the blind Templar dead rise and ride. The monastery is owned by the town, has been partly consolidated and can be visited on scheduled tours.

title: Fornells, Menorca (Who Can Kill a Child 1976)
description: The whitewashed fishing harbour of Fornells on Menorca's north coast is the mainland port from which Tom and Evelyn set out for the island of Almanzora. Fornells is still a working harbour village.

title: Sitges, Catalonia (Who Can Kill a Child 1976)
description: The seaside scenes in the crowded Spanish resort that opens the film were shot in Sitges, south of Barcelona. The town later became home to Spain's biggest fantasy and horror festival.

title: Ciruelos, Toledo (Who Can Kill a Child 1976)
description: Much of the deserted island village, far from any sea, was actually the inland town of Ciruelos in Toledo province. It remains a small working agricultural town.

title: El Cubillo de Uceda, Guadalajara (The Devil's Backbone 2001)
description: Del Toro built the Santa Lucia orphanage and its courtyard with the bomb in it on open country near this Guadalajara village. The village is a small farming settlement north of Madrid and the set has since been removed.

title: Talamanca de Jarama, Madrid (The Devil's Backbone 2001)
description: Further exteriors for the orphanage story were shot around this old walled town on the Jarama river. Talamanca has a medieval bridge and Romanesque church and is open to walk around.

title: San Rafael, Segovia (Pan's Labyrinth 2006)
description: The mill that Vidal takes over, and the Scots pine woods around it where Ofelia finds the labyrinth, were built and shot in the Guadarrama mountains near San Rafael. The set was struck after filming, but the pine forest and the village are still there.

title: Lake Inba, Chiba (Onibaba 1964)
description: Kaneto Shindo shot the entire film in the towering susuki grass on a riverbank beside the Inba marsh, housing his crew in prefab huts on the spot for the summer. The lake is still there in Chiba Prefecture with public paths and cycle routes along its banks.

title: Gokseong County, Jeolla (The Wailing 2016)
description: Na Hong-jin named his film after this mountain and river county in South Jeolla and shot a large part of it here, out of 97 location days across Korea. Gokseong is a farming county served by its own railway station.

title: Rue Georges et Xavier Schlumberger, Marnes-la-Coquette (Eyes Without a Face 1960)
description: Doctor Genessier's gated mansion, where his daughter waits in a mask, stands on this lane in a wealthy village west of Paris. It is a private home set well back behind trees, so there is little to see from the street.

title: Chateau du Haut du Bel Air, Le Chesnay (Eyes Without a Face 1960)
description: The surgeon's clinic, where the face transplants are carried out, was this chateau on the rue de Versailles. The building is barely changed but now sits inside the campus of a special education service, so it is not open to visitors.

title: Place Paul Painleve, Paris (Eyes Without a Face 1960)
description: Louise trawls for young women with the right face near the Sorbonne, and is seen on this small square beside the Musee de Cluny. The square is a public garden with a statue and benches.

title: Institut medico-legal, Paris (Diabolique 1955)
description: The morgue sequence, where the wife is taken to identify a body, was shot in the real Paris forensic institute on the Seine by the Pont d'Austerlitz. It is still the city morgue and is not open to the public.

title: Montfort-l'Amaury, Yvelines (Diabolique 1955)
description: Nicole's house, written as being in Niort, was actually filmed in this hill town west of Paris, opposite a building Clouzot had already used in Le Corbeau. Montfort-l'Amaury is a small tourist town with a ruined castle above it.

title: L'Etang-la-Ville, Yvelines (Diabolique 1955)
description: Clouzot spent five weeks shooting the boarding school, and its notorious swimming pool, at a run down chateau in this village between Saint-Cloud and Saint-Germain. The village is on the Paris suburban rail network.

title: Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, University of Liege (Raw 2016)
description: Julia Ducournau shot her cannibal coming of age story on this 1970s concrete veterinary campus at Sart Tilman, having found no French vet school with the American style layout she wanted. It is a working university faculty, so visitors should keep to public areas.

title: Sheffield Park, East Sussex (The Innocents 1961)
description: The Gothic mansion here played Bly, the house where the governess starts seeing figures at the windows, with interiors built at Shepperton. The house is privately owned, but the surrounding garden and lake are National Trust and open to visitors.

title: Newman Passage, London (Peeping Tom 1960)
description: Mark follows his first victim down this narrow covered alley off Rathbone Street with the camera running under his coat. The passage is a public right of way in Fitzrovia and looks much as it did in 1960.

title: The Newman Arms, London (Peeping Tom 1960)
description: Dora takes Mark up to her room above this Fitzrovia pub, where he films her death. The Newman Arms is still trading at 23 Rathbone Street.

title: Melbury Road, Kensington (Peeping Tom 1960)
description: Mark's house, with the darkroom and the home movies of his father's experiments, was 5 Melbury Road. Number 5 was demolished and replaced by a block of flats, though its neighbour at number 7 and Michael Powell's own house at number 8 still stand.

title: Market Place, Lavenham (Witchfinder General 1968)
description: The witch burning and the crowd scenes were staged in the market square of this Suffolk wool town, whose crooked timber houses needed almost no dressing. The square is open and the Guildhall on it is National Trust.

title: Kentwell Hall, Long Melford (Witchfinder General 1968)
description: The moated Tudor hall stood in for the place where the accused are tried and John Lowes is hanged. Kentwell is privately owned but opens to the public for much of the year.

title: Orford Castle, Suffolk (Witchfinder General 1968)
description: The cellar of this twelfth century keep is where Hopkins takes Richard Marshall to be tortured, and where Hopkins is shot and hacked apart. The castle is run by English Heritage and visitors can climb to the roof.

title: Black Park, Buckinghamshire (The Devil Rides Out 1968)
description: The clearing where the Satanists summon the Goat of Mendes was shot in Black Park, the pine woodland next to Pinewood Studios that Hammer used again and again. It is a country park with free public access and a car park.

title: High Canons, Well End (The Devil Rides Out 1968)
description: The Georgian house at High Canons on Buckettsland Lane was Mocata's home. It is a private house used for filming, so it should only be seen from the lane.

title: The Manor Elstree, former Edgwarebury Hotel (The Devil Rides Out 1968)
description: The Eatons' country house, where the characters sit out the night inside the chalk circle, was the Edgwarebury Hotel at Elstree. The building is now a hotel called The Manor Elstree.

title: CityPoint, Ropemaker Street, London (28 Weeks Later 2007)
description: Most of the fortified District One, where returning survivors are housed under army guard, was shot around the CityPoint tower near Moorgate rather than in Canary Wharf itself. The tower is a working office block with a public plaza at its base.

title: Charing Cross station, London (28 Weeks Later 2007)
description: The film used the mainline station and the Underground beneath it for the evacuation and the pitch black tunnel sequence. Charing Cross is an active station in daily use.

title: Wembley Stadium, London (28 Weeks Later 2007)
description: The empty stadium appears in the sweep over an abandoned London, filmed while the rebuilt Wembley was newly finished. It is open for stadium tours and events.

title: Trafalgar Square, London (28 Weeks Later 2007)
description: The production closed central London at dawn to shoot the deserted square, part of the sequence of an emptied capital. The square is public and open at all hours.

title: Canary Wharf DLR station, London (28 Weeks Later 2007)
description: The Docklands Light Railway and its arrival at Canary Wharf feature in the scenes of the repopulated safe zone. The station is on the working DLR network.

title: San Nicolo dei Mendicoli, Venice (Don't Look Now 1973)
description: This twelfth century church in a quiet corner of Dorsoduro is the one John Baxter has come to Venice to restore, and where he falls from the scaffolding. It is still a parish church and is usually open to visitors.

title: Hotel Gabrielli, Venice (Don't Look Now 1973)
description: The exterior and lobby of the Baxters' Hotel Europa were filmed at the Gabrielli on the Riva degli Schiavoni. The hotel is still operating on the waterfront.

title: Bauer Palazzo, Venice (Don't Look Now 1973)
description: The interiors of the fictional Hotel Europa, including the much discussed love scene, were shot at the Bauer Grunwald near Piazza San Marco. The building still stands as the Bauer Palazzo, which has been closed for a long redevelopment.

title: Palazzo Grimani di Santa Maria Formosa, Venice (Don't Look Now 1973)
description: The palazzo where Baxter finally corners the small figure in the red coat stands beside Santa Maria Formosa. It is now a state museum open to ticketed visitors.

title: Point Reyes Lighthouse (The Fog 1980)
description: The 1870 lighthouse and its long descending stairway stood in for the Antonio Bay light that houses Stevie Wayne's radio station KAB. It is still a National Park Service site inside Point Reyes National Seashore and open to visitors on posted days.

title: Stevie Wayne's house, 12830 Sir Francis Drake Boulevard (The Fog 1980)
description: Adrienne Barbeau's character lives here in the film, on the road running north through Inverness along Tomales Bay. This is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE: view it from the road and do not approach the house.

title: Drakes Beach, Point Reyes National Seashore (The Fog 1980)
description: The wide pale-cliffed beach used for the film's shoreline scenes. It is a public beach with a visitor center and remains almost unchanged.

title: The Tides Wharf, Bodega Bay (The Fog 1980)
description: The working fishing wharf served as the Antonio Bay docks where the Sea Grass crew meets the fog. The Tides is still a restaurant and fish market on Highway 1, and the same wharf appears in Hitchcock's The Birds.

title: Episcopal Church of the Ascension, Sierra Madre (The Fog 1980)
description: Father Malone's church, built in 1888 and on the National Register of Historic Places, sits 400 miles south of the Marin County coast the rest of the film was shot on. It is still an active parish, and the driveway seen in the film has been removed.

title: Shoreline Highway, Point Reyes Station (The Fog 1980)
description: The main street of this one-block town played the streets of Antonio Bay. The storefronts are still recognizable and the town remains a working ranching and tourist stop.

title: Canyon Country Store, Laurel Canyon (The Fog 1980)
description: The Laurel Canyon landmark grocery appears in the film's Los Angeles pickup shots. It is still an operating market and deli.

title: Olema, California (The Fog 1980)
description: The village on Highway 1 at the mouth of Olema Valley was used for the centennial statue unveiling sequence. It is still a tiny crossroads settlement with an inn and a general store.

title: Salmon Glacier, British Columbia (The Thing 1982)
description: Outpost 31, the American research station, was built as a full standing set on the ice about 15 miles north of Stewart. The set is long gone but the glacier is still reachable by the Salmon Glacier road in summer.

title: Stewart, British Columbia (The Thing 1982)
description: This isolated port town was the production base and the site of the exterior American and Norwegian camp sets. Both camps were built for the film and no longer exist.

title: Universal Studios Hollywood (The Thing 1982)
description: All the station interiors were shot on refrigerated soundstages here, chilled to about 40 degrees so the actors' breath would show. The lot is still a working studio and theme park.

title: Union Center for the Arts, 120 Judge John Aiso Street (Prince of Darkness 1987)
description: The Little Tokyo building that plays the abandoned church holding the cylinder of green liquid. Long the Japanese Union Church of Los Angeles, it is now the East West Players theatre and arts center.

title: Mission San Fernando Rey de Espana (Prince of Darkness 1987)
description: The 1797 mission appears in the opening sequence as the priest's order receives the dying man's key. It is still an active Catholic site with a museum open to the public.

title: Town and Gown, University of Southern California (Prince of Darkness 1987)
description: Professor Birack's university scenes were shot around this USC building on Exposition Boulevard. It is still a campus event hall.

title: Crystal Ballroom, Millennium Biltmore Hotel (They Live 1988)
description: The aliens' shareholder banquet, where Nada and Frank crash the party, was staged in the Biltmore's ornate ballroom. The 1923 hotel is still open and the ballroom is still rented for events.

title: 650 South Spring Street, Downtown Los Angeles (They Live 1988)
description: The bank at 7th and Spring is where Roddy Piper walks in with a shotgun and delivers the bubblegum line. The building still stands in the Historic Core and now holds ground-floor retail.

title: Holly's house, 8634 Franklin Avenue (They Live 1988)
description: The hillside home where Nada forces Holly Thompson to hide him, and where she puts him through a window. This is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE on a narrow street: look from the sidewalk and never knock.

title: Baltimore Hotel, 501 South Los Angeles Street (They Live 1988)
description: The cheap downtown hotel where Nada and Frank hole up after the alley fight. The building survives on Gallery Row and still operates as low-cost housing.

title: 1216 West 7th Street grocery (They Live 1988)
description: The corner market at 7th and Garland is where Nada first sees the ghouls behind the sunglasses and starts shooting. The storefront is still a neighborhood liquor and grocery store.

title: Los Angeles City Hall lawn (They Live 1988)
description: The park beside City Hall on 1st at Spring is where the blind street preacher rails about the ones who control everything. The lawn is now part of Grand Park and is open to the public.

title: Cathedral of the Transfiguration, Markham (In the Mouth of Madness 1994)
description: The Byzantine-style Slovak cathedral, with its tall bell tower, is the black church of Hobb's End. The building still stands in Markham's Cathedraltown but has been closed and deconsecrated.

title: West Montrose Covered Bridge, Ontario (In the Mouth of Madness 1994)
description: Ontario's last surviving covered bridge, built in 1881, is the crossing Trent and Linda pass through on the night ride into Hobb's End. It is still open to one lane of traffic over the Grand River.

title: The Unionville Arms, 189 Main Street Unionville (In the Mouth of Madness 1994)
description: This pub on Unionville's heritage main street is the Hobb's End bar exterior. It is still a working pub and the street's nineteenth-century frontages are largely intact.

title: R.C. Harris Water Treatment Plant, Toronto (In the Mouth of Madness 1994)
description: The Art Deco waterworks on the Scarborough bluffs plays the exterior of the mental hospital where John Trent is locked up. It is a working treatment plant and the grounds are open as public parkland.

title: Eglinton Theatre, 400 Eglinton Avenue West (In the Mouth of Madness 1994)
description: The 1936 Art Deco cinema is where Trent sits laughing at the film of his own story in the final scene. It closed as a movie house in 2002 and is now the Eglinton Grand event venue.

title: Point Reyes Station as Midwich (Village of the Damned 1995)
description: Carpenter came back to the town he used in The Fog and made its main street the town of Midwich, including the blackout sequence. The storefronts are still standing and largely unchanged.

title: McGowan house, 281 B Street, Point Reyes Station (Village of the Damned 1995)
description: The home of Christopher Reeve's Dr. Alan Chaffee and his family sits a block off the main street. This is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE: look from the sidewalk and do not knock.

title: Nicasio School, 5555 Nicasio Valley Road (Village of the Damned 1995)
description: The town picnic and school fair scenes were shot at this one-room-style country school in Nicasio Valley. It is still an operating public elementary school, so keep to the road.

title: Garage at 12786 Sir Francis Drake Boulevard, Inverness (Village of the Damned 1995)
description: John Carpenter takes his own cameo as a garage attendant at this spot in Inverness. The building is still in commercial use on the main road through town.

title: Church of the Assumption, Tomales (Village of the Damned 1995)
description: The white wooden church and its hillside graveyard in Tomales were used for the cemetery scenes. The church is still standing above the village on Church Street.

title: Historic Plaza Hotel, Las Vegas, New Mexico (Vampires 1998)
description: The 1882 hotel on the old town plaza is where Jack Crow and the turning Katrina hole up. It is still an operating hotel and has since appeared in No Country for Old Men.

title: Los Cerrillos, New Mexico (Vampires 1998)
description: This former mining village on the Turquoise Trail stands in for the town of Santiago, and a large territorial prison set was built nearby. Cerrillos is still a tiny inhabited village with a dirt main street.

title: Eastern State Hospital, Medical Lake, Washington (The Ward 2010)
description: Carpenter shot the North Bend Psychiatric Hospital scenes inside this state psychiatric facility west of Spokane, using older wards that were out of service. It remains an active state hospital and is not open to visitors.

title: Eastern Washington University, Cheney (The Ward 2010)
description: Additional interiors for Carpenter's last feature were shot on the EWU campus in Cheney. The university is still in operation.

title: Sepulveda Dam, Los Angeles (Escape from New York 1981)
description: The 1941 flood-control dam is the brutalist concrete structure standing in for the air traffic control center and the fortified bridge out of Manhattan. It is still in place in the Sepulveda Basin and visible from the recreation area.

title: ArtCenter College of Design Hillside Campus, Pasadena (Escape from New York 1981)
description: The long steel-and-glass building on Lida Street gave the film its cold institutional corridors during Snake Plissken's briefing. It is still an active art and design college campus.

title: The Wiltern, 3790 Wilshire Boulevard (Escape from New York 1981)
description: The 1931 Wiltern Theatre and its basement supplied interiors for the World Trade Center sequences. It was saved from demolition in the 1980s and now operates as a concert venue.

title: Fabulous Fox Theatre, St. Louis (Escape from New York 1981)
description: The Fox facade appears as a derelict Broadway theatre, and it was genuinely rundown when the crew shot it. It has since been fully restored and is one of the busiest theatres in the Midwest.

title: New Masonic Temple, 3681 Lindell Boulevard, St. Louis (Escape from New York 1981)
description: The columned Masonic temple stood in for the New York Public Library that Plissken searches for the President. The Masons sold the building in 2014 and it has been converted to apartments.

title: St. Louis Union Station (Escape from New York 1981)
description: The disused train sheds and the Grand Hall provided the railway scenes and a major fight. The station has since been converted into a hotel, aquarium and retail complex.

title: Old Chain of Rocks Bridge, St. Louis (Escape from New York 1981)
description: The mined 69th Street Bridge that Plissken drives across in the finale is this kinked 1929 span over the Mississippi. It was closed to cars in 1968 and reopened in 1999 as a pedestrian and bicycle bridge on Route 66.

title: Doheny Memorial Library, USC (Escape from New York 1981)
description: The lobby of USC's 1932 main library doubled for the interior of the New York Public Library. It is still the university's central library.

title: Century Plaza Towers, Century City (Escape from New York 1981)
description: The twin triangular towers stand in for the entrance to the World Trade Center in the film's opening. Both towers still dominate the Century City skyline.

title: Crickadarn, Powys, Wales (An American Werewolf in London 1981)
description: The exterior of the Slaughtered Lamb, complete with the red phone box, is a cottage in this Welsh village standing in for East Proctor. The hanging Angel of Death sign was a prop, and the cottage is now a restored PRIVATE RESIDENCE: view from the lane only.

title: The Black Swan, Martyr's Green, Surrey (An American Werewolf in London 1981)
description: The interior of the Slaughtered Lamb, with the five-pointed star on the wall and the darts game that stops dead, was shot in this Surrey pub. It is still open, now as a smarter restaurant-pub, and the layout is recognizable.

title: Piccadilly Circus, London (An American Werewolf in London 1981)
description: The pile-up finale was shot here across two nights between 1 and 4 in the morning, the first film permitted to close the Circus in fifteen years. The junction is still a landmark, though the Eros cinema where David hides was demolished and the corner is now a clothing store.

title: Tottenham Court Road Underground station (An American Werewolf in London 1981)
description: The escalator and tunnel chase in which a commuter is hunted down was filmed here outside service hours. The station is still open and was heavily rebuilt for Crossrail.

title: ZSL London Zoo, Regent's Park (An American Werewolf in London 1981)
description: David wakes up naked in the wolf enclosure here the morning after his first transformation. The zoo is still open, although the terraces used in the scene have been rebuilt.

title: Trafalgar Square, London (An American Werewolf in London 1981)
description: David leaps out of a taxi here after hearing the news reports of the killings. The square was pedestrianized on its north side in 2003 but is otherwise as filmed.

title: Coleherne Road, Earl's Court (An American Werewolf in London 1981)
description: Nurse Alex Price's flat, where the second transformation happens, is in a terrace on this Earl's Court street. These are PRIVATE RESIDENCES: look from the pavement and do not ring any bells.

title: The Pryors, East Heath Road, Hampstead (An American Werewolf in London 1981)
description: The grand red-brick mansion block beside Hampstead Heath is where the werewolf attacks a resident. It is still a PRIVATE apartment building: view it from East Heath Road.

title: Clink Street, Southwark (An American Werewolf in London 1981)
description: The dead-end alley of the final confrontation was created here, with a false wall built across the street. The street layout survives but the warehouses have been rebuilt into flats and the Clink Prison Museum sits nearby.

title: Hay Bluff, Black Mountains, Wales (An American Werewolf in London 1981)
description: The bleak open moor where David and Jack are dropped off and told to stick to the road was shot on the high ground near Hay Bluff. It is still open access land with a car park at the foot of the bluff.

title: Mendocino Woodlands State Park (The Howling 1981)
description: Joe Dante took over Camp 2, the most remote of the three 1930s work camps here, to shoot the Colony where the werewolves live. The camps are still standing and can be rented as group retreats.

title: Russian Gulch State Park, Mendocino County (The Howling 1981)
description: The redwood forest running and chase footage was shot in the coastal woods just north of Mendocino village. It is still a state park open for day use and camping.

title: Paradise Cove, Malibu (The Howling 1981)
description: The beach campfire sequence when Karen first arrives at the Colony was shot at this Malibu cove. It is a private beach club and parking lot but remains accessible for a fee.

title: 6607 Hollywood Boulevard (The Howling 1981)
description: The adult bookstore where Karen goes looking for Eddie Quist was this Hollywood Boulevard storefront. The block has been heavily redeveloped and the shop is long gone.

title: Courthouse Square, Universal Studios backlot (Gremlins 1984)
description: Kingston Falls, including the snowy town square and the theatre full of gremlins, is this 1948 standing set on the Universal backlot, better known as Hill Valley from Back to the Future. Most of the square has burned and been rebuilt twice since 1984, though the courthouse itself survived.

title: Warner Bros. Studios, Burbank (Gremlins 1984)
description: The Peltzer house interiors and much of the gremlin puppetry work were done on soundstages at the Warner lot, with the town exteriors shot up the hill at Universal. The studio still runs public tours.

title: Walt Disney Studios, Burbank (Fright Night 1985)
description: The Brewster and Dandrige houses were built as facades on the Disney lot's Residential Street set so the crew could get crane shots down the block. That set was torn down in 1991 to make room for soundstages, so nothing of Fright Night's street survives.

title: The Culver Studios, Culver City (Fright Night 1985)
description: Known as Laird International Studios when Fright Night shot there, this lot held the house interiors and duplicate exteriors built by production designer John De Cuir Jr. The studio is still operating under its original Culver Studios name.

title: Uneeda Medical Supply, 698 Moulton Avenue (The Return of the Living Dead 1985)
description: The warehouse where Frank and Freddy crack open the army drum is this brick industrial building in Lincoln Heights, and the Resurrection Cemetery gate was built by the crew at the end of the same street. The building still stands in a working industrial district.

title: West Los Angeles VA Medical Center (Re-Animator 1985)
description: The Wilshire Boulevard veterans hospital provided the exterior of Miskatonic University Medical School. It is still an active VA medical campus.

title: Dan Cain's house, 2238 Canyon Drive (Re-Animator 1985)
description: The house Dan Cain rents and where Herbert West sets up his basement lab. This is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE on a narrow canyon street: view it from the road only.

title: Dean Halsey's house, 405 South Irving Boulevard (Re-Animator 1985)
description: The Windsor Square home of Dean Halsey and his daughter Megan. This is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE in a historic district: look from the sidewalk and do not approach.

title: Occidental Studios, 201 North Occidental Boulevard (Re-Animator 1985)
description: The morgue and laboratory sets, including the reanimation scenes, were built on stages at this small independent studio near Echo Park. It is one of the oldest continuously operating studio lots in Los Angeles.

title: 1901 Venice Boulevard (Re-Animator 1985)
description: The opening University of Zurich sequence, where West's first experiment goes wrong, was shot at this building on Venice Boulevard, now Loyola High School. The campus is still in use as a school.

title: 716 West 28th Street sorority house (Night of the Creeps 1986)
description: The main Corman University sorority house is one of the old fraternity row houses just north of USC. These are PRIVATE student houses: view from the sidewalk.

title: Haines Hall, UCLA (Night of the Creeps 1986)
description: Campus scenes at Corman University were shot in front of this 1929 Romanesque building on UCLA's original quad. It is still an academic building and the quad is open to visitors.

title: California State University Northridge (Night of the Creeps 1986)
description: Further Corman University campus footage was shot on the CSUN campus in the San Fernando Valley. The university is still in operation, though much of it was rebuilt after the 1994 Northridge earthquake.

title: Coolidge, Arizona (Near Dark 1987)
description: Kathryn Bigelow moved the production here after flooding wrecked the Oklahoma plan, and the town's streets carry the opening night driving montage and the Severen truck sequence. Coolidge is still a small farming town on the Gila River.

title: Randolph, Arizona (Near Dark 1987)
description: The tiny settlement south of Coolidge is where Jesse parks the stolen RV during the day. Randolph remains a scattering of houses among the cotton fields.

title: 6709 Pacific Boulevard, Huntington Park (Near Dark 1987)
description: Caleb's walk to the bus station was shot on this busy shopping street in Huntington Park. Pacific Boulevard is still a dense retail corridor.

title: Magdalen Square, Abbeville, Louisiana (The Blob 1988)
description: Abbeville's central square plays the town of Arborville, California, and is where most of the street-level chaos was filmed. The square is still the heart of the Abbeville Commercial Historic District and the town screens the film here.

title: Frank's Theater, 108 South Jefferson Street, Abbeville (The Blob 1988)
description: The movie house where the blob comes through the projection booth and the audience is trapped. The building is still on South Jefferson Street but no longer operates as a cinema.

title: 117 South Jefferson Street, Abbeville (The Blob 1988)
description: Brian rounds the corner of the Bank of Abbeville building in one of the film's chase beats. The bank building still stands in the historic commercial district.

title: Vermilion Parish Courthouse, Abbeville (The Blob 1988)
description: The courthouse appears in the Arborville town scenes on the edge of the square. It is still the working parish courthouse.

title: Vermilion Catholic High School, Abbeville (The Blob 1988)
description: The high school and its adjacent football field were used for the school and game sequences. Both are still in use by the school.

title: Mentryville, Pico Canyon (Pumpkinhead 1988)
description: The Harley grocery gate and the surrounding backroad country were shot at this preserved 1890s oil boomtown in Pico Canyon above Santa Clarita. Mentryville is now a park site with the Felton schoolhouse and the Mentry house still standing.

title: Tournament House, 391 South Orange Grove Boulevard, Pasadena (Society 1989)
description: The Wrigley Mansion on Pasadena's old Millionaires Row is the house where the shunting party takes place. It is now the Tournament of Roses headquarters and offers free public tours in season.

title: Birmingham High School, Van Nuys (Society 1989)
description: Bill Whitney's school scenes were shot at this San Fernando Valley campus. It now operates as Birmingham Community Charter High School.

title: Alabama Hills, Lone Pine (Tremors 1990)
description: The boulder outcrops where Val and Earl run from the graboids are these weathered granite hills below Mount Whitney, a location used in Westerns since the 1920s. The area is now a designated National Scenic Area with open public access.

title: Olancha, California (Tremors 1990)
description: The town of Perfection was built from scratch on the flats off Cactus Flat Road east of Olancha. The set was torn down after filming, leaving only the dirt road and a replica City of Perfection sign put up by fans.

title: Darwin, California (Tremors 1990)
description: Parts of the film were shot in this near-ghost town in the hills above Panamint Valley, and residents have kept a small museum of Tremors material. Darwin still has a handful of inhabitants and no services.

title: Richland Avenue Elementary School, Los Angeles (The Monster Squad 1987)
description: The school scenes, including E.J. bullying Horace in the back courtyard, were shot at this West Los Angeles elementary school. It is still an operating public school, so keep to the sidewalk.

title: Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County (The Monster Squad 1987)
description: The museum sequence where the kids hunt for the amulet was shot inside this 1913 Exposition Park landmark. The museum is still open to the public.

title: Warner Bros. Ranch, Burbank (The Monster Squad 1987)
description: Sean's house and most of the neighborhood were facades on the Warner Bros. Ranch backlot, the same standing street later used for Bewitched and Lethal Weapon. The ranch was sold in 2019 and the residential sets have since been cleared.

title: Mills View, 329 Melrose Avenue, Monrovia (House 1986)
description: Roger Cobb's inherited haunted house is this 1887 Victorian in Monrovia, which the crew repainted, fenced and spiked with roof spires for the shoot. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE: view it from Melrose Avenue and do not knock.

title: Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk (Killer Klowns from Outer Space 1988)
description: The amusement park where the klowns' circus tent spaceship lifts off in the finale. The 1907 boardwalk is still open and still runs the Giant Dipper coaster seen in the film.

title: Big Top Burger, 300 East Lake Avenue, Watsonville (Killer Klowns from Outer Space 1988)
description: The burger stand in Crescent Cove was this East Lake Avenue drive-in in Watsonville. The building is still a fast food stand on the same corner.

title: Crescent Cove police station, 231 Union Street, Watsonville (Killer Klowns from Outer Space 1988)
description: Officer Mooney's station house, where Dave works and the klowns eventually turn up, is this civic building in downtown Watsonville. It still stands near the city plaza.

title: Debbie Stone's house, 615 California Street, Santa Cruz (Killer Klowns from Outer Space 1988)
description: The home of the film's heroine, where the klowns pull their shadow-puppet trick. This is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE: look from the sidewalk only.

title: Watsonville Plaza gazebo, 358 Main Street (Killer Klowns from Outer Space 1988)
description: The town park and bandstand where the klowns walk through Crescent Cove in daylight. The plaza and its gazebo are still the center of downtown Watsonville.

title: New Brighton State Beach, Capitola (Killer Klowns from Outer Space 1988)
description: Coastal scenes for Crescent Cove were shot at this state beach south of Santa Cruz. It is still open for day use and camping.

title: Sherman Oaks Galleria (Chopping Mall 1986)
description: The killbot rampage was shot after hours in the enclosed Sherman Oaks Galleria, the mall that also defined Valley Girl and Fast Times at Ridgemont High. The indoor mall closed in 1999 after earthquake damage and was rebuilt as an open-air retail and office center, so the interiors from the film no longer exist.

title: Beverly Center, Los Angeles (Chopping Mall 1986)
description: The Park Plaza Mall exteriors were shot at the Beverly Center, which had originally been the planned location for the whole film. The mall is still open and was given a major redesign in 2018.

title: Dunsmuir House, Oakland (Phantasm 1979)
description: The white-columned mansion on this estate is Morningside Mortuary, the Tall Man's funeral home, though the interiors were sets built elsewhere. The house and gardens are a City of Oakland historic site open for tours and events.

title: Mike and Jody's house, 1232 Corsica Drive (Phantasm 1979)
description: The brothers' home in Don Coscarelli's film sits on a quiet Pacific Palisades street. This is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE: view from the sidewalk and do not knock.

title: Fortune teller's house, 22840 Calvert Street, Woodland Hills (Phantasm 1979)
description: The house where the old woman and the girl read Mike's fortune and the black box test happens. This is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE: look from the street only.

title: 1824 West Main Street, Alhambra (Phantasm 1979)
description: The interior of Reggie's ice cream shop was filmed in this West Main Street storefront in Alhambra. The building remains in commercial use.

title: Carla Moran's house, 523 Sheldon Street, El Segundo (The Entity 1982)
description: The house where Barbara Hershey's character is attacked by the unseen presence. This is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE: view it from the sidewalk and never knock.

title: 2586 North Beachwood Drive (The Entity 1982)
description: This 1930 Beachwood Canyon house was used for the second home in the film. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE on a narrow hillside street: look from the road only.

title: The Culver Studios, Culver City (The Entity 1982)
description: Then called Laird International Studios, this lot housed the stage work including the plaster-cast laboratory climax. It still operates as The Culver Studios.

title: Celtic Street, Chatsworth (Poltergeist II: The Other Side 1986)
description: The ruined Cuesta Verde of the opening credits was staged on Celtic Street, where the crew put up false-front houses and a condemned sign beside the empty lot standing in for the Freeling home. The street is now fully built out with ordinary houses, so nothing of the set remains.

title: Spider Rock, Canyon de Chelly (Poltergeist II: The Other Side 1986)
description: The twin sandstone spire that Taylor and the family visit in the Navajo Nation sequences rises 750 feet from the canyon floor. It is viewed from the Spider Rock Overlook on the South Rim Drive, and the canyon floor itself can only be entered with a Navajo guide.

title: 875 North Michigan Avenue, Chicago (Poltergeist III 1988)
description: The black cross-braced tower where Carol Anne stays with her aunt and uncle, and where the mirrors turn against everyone, is the former John Hancock Center. It still stands on the Magnificent Mile and the observation deck is open as 360 Chicago.

title: Water Tower Place, Chicago (Poltergeist III 1988)
description: The crossing escalators in the mall sequence were shot at Water Tower Place, directly across Michigan Avenue from the Hancock tower. The mall is still open, although many of its upper floors have emptied out.

title: 1435 North Astor Street, Chicago (Poltergeist III 1988)
description: Carol Anne's school was shot at this building on the Gold Coast's Astor Street, a block of protected nineteenth-century mansions. The block is PRIVATE property: walk the sidewalk and do not enter any gate.

title: Pender County Courthouse square, Burgaw (Silver Bullet 1985)
description: The Tarker's Mills town festival was staged around the 1936 courthouse in the middle of Burgaw. The courthouse and square are still the center of the town.

title: Ideal Barber Shop, 105 South Wright Street, Burgaw (Silver Bullet 1985)
description: One of the Tarker's Mills storefronts a block from the courthouse. The barber shop building is still standing in Burgaw's small downtown.

title: Greenfield Lake, Wilmington (Silver Bullet 1985)
description: The fireworks scene where Marty meets the werewolf on a bridge was shot at this cypress lake in Wilmington, and the search party and gazebo scenes were filmed in the surrounding park. The bridge used in the film has since been torn down, but the lake and its loop trail are open to the public.

title: Dick Morrison's house, 314 South Front Street, Wilmington (Cat's Eye 1985)
description: The home of James Woods's character in the Quitters, Inc. segment. This is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE in Wilmington's historic district: look from the sidewalk and do not knock.

title: 125 South 3rd Street, Wilmington (Cat's Eye 1985)
description: Saint Stephen's School for the Exceptional, where Morrison's daughter is a student, was shot at this downtown Wilmington building. It still stands in the historic district.

title: Isabel Holmes Bridge, Wilmington (Cat's Eye 1985)
description: The lift bridge over the Northeast Cape Fear River appears in the Quitters, Inc. segment. It is still carrying US 74 traffic into downtown Wilmington.

title: Isabel Holmes Bridge, Wilmington (Maximum Overdrive 1986)
description: The drawbridge that opens on its own early in the film, throwing cars and a watermelon truck around, is this Wilmington lift bridge. It is still in service on US 74.

title: 361 Willow Hedge Drive, Monroeville (Creepshow 1982)
description: The suburban house where Billy's father throws away the horror comic in the wraparound story. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE in a Monroeville neighborhood whose owners get regular fan traffic: view it from the street and do not knock.

title: Margaret Morrison Carnegie Hall, Carnegie Mellon University (Creepshow 1982)
description: The university basement where the crate is found in The Crate was shot in this rotunda-fronted 1907 building in Pittsburgh. It is still a working CMU academic building.

title: Island Beach State Park, New Jersey (Creepshow 1982)
description: Something to Tide You Over, in which Leslie Nielsen buries two people up to their necks in the sand, was shot on this barrier-island beach. The park is still open for swimming and surf fishing.

title: Redford Theatre (It Follows 2014)
description: Jay's date with Hugh happens inside this 1928 atmospheric movie palace on Lahser Road, where she first spots a woman nobody else can see. It still runs classic films with organ shows, staffed by volunteers.

title: Jay's house, 38721 Trafalgar Way (It Follows 2014)
description: The Height family home, with the above-ground backyard pool and the bedroom where Jay watches the street. This is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE on a quiet Sterling Heights cul-de-sac.

title: Annie's house, 1492 Yorkshire Road (It Follows 2014)
description: The house in the cold open, where the first girl runs out into the street in heels before driving to the beach. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE in Birmingham, Michigan.

title: Greg's house, 5222 Allison Drive (It Follows 2014)
description: Greg's home across the subdivision, seen from Jay's bedroom window and used for the film's most brutal reveal. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE in Troy, Michigan.

title: Nick's Country Oven, Clawson (It Follows 2014)
description: The diner-style restaurant on West 14 Mile Road where the friends regroup over food. It is still an operating family restaurant.

title: Clark's Ice Cream, Berkley (It Follows 2014)
description: The ice cream shop on 12 Mile Road that the characters visit in daylight, a deliberate piece of ordinary suburbia in a film about being followed. It is still a working ice cream stand.

title: Clawson High School pool (It Follows 2014)
description: The indoor swimming pool where the climax was shot, with the plan to electrocute the entity in the water. It is a working high school, so the pool is not open to visitors.

title: Water Works Park, Detroit (It Follows 2014)
description: The kids walk toward the pool building through Detroit's Water Works Park on East Jefferson, whose high lift pumping station provides the exterior. The park grounds are city water department property and largely closed to the public.

title: Adelaide Studios, Glenside (The Babadook 2014)
description: Amelia's Victorian terrace, including the basement and the hallway that swallows the light, was built as a set on the sound stage here. The Babadook was the first feature to shoot in the South Australian Film Corporation's new studios.

title: Adelaide Studios, Glenside (Bring Her Back 2025)
description: The Philippou brothers shot their second feature in South Australia, with studio work at the SAFC's Adelaide Studios and locations around Adelaide. The same stages built the house in The Babadook a decade earlier.

title: Taft, California (A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night 2014)
description: This small Kern County oil town, about 30 miles southwest of Bakersfield, played the Iranian ghost town of Bad City in Ana Lily Amirpour's black and white vampire western. The nodding pumpjacks and empty streets were shot in and around town.

title: Westminster Bridge (28 Days Later 2002)
description: Jim crosses the empty bridge toward the Houses of Parliament in the film's most copied image. The crew held traffic for a few minutes at a time in the early hours on Sundays to get it.

title: Horse Guards Parade (28 Days Later 2002)
description: Part of Jim's walk through a deserted central London after he wakes in the hospital. The parade ground is open to the public and still used for ceremonial duties.

title: Shaftesbury Memorial Fountain, Piccadilly Circus (28 Days Later 2002)
description: The fountain, commonly called Eros, appears boarded up and covered in missing person notices. It sits in the middle of Piccadilly Circus and is one of the easiest shots in the film to stand in.

title: Centre Point, New Oxford Street (28 Days Later 2002)
description: The 1960s tower at St Giles Circus features in the abandoned West End sequence. It was converted into apartments in the 2010s.

title: Royal Exchange, City of London (28 Days Later 2002)
description: Jim wanders through the deserted financial district past the Royal Exchange on Cornhill. The building now houses shops and restaurants under its portico.

title: St Anne's Church, Limehouse (28 Days Later 2002)
description: The Hawksmoor church where Jim finds bodies in the pews and is attacked by the infected priest. It is a working parish church in Tower Hamlets.

title: Limehouse Link tunnel (28 Days Later 2002)
description: The tunnel chase, with the taxi reversing away from the infected in the dark, was shot here rather than the Blackwall Tunnel. It is a busy road tunnel, so this one is for looking at from street level.

title: 145 Tottenham Court Road (28 Days Later 2002)
description: The supermarket looting scene, where the survivors calmly stock up on single malt, was shot in what was then a Budgens. The shop has since become a Lidl.

title: Central Middlesex Hospital, Acton Lane (28 Days Later 2002)
description: Part of the deserted hospital where Jim wakes from his coma, cut together with the now demolished Greenwich District Hospital. Central Middlesex is still an NHS hospital site.

title: Waverley Abbey, Surrey (28 Days Later 2002)
description: The ruined Cistercian abbey near Farnham where the group rests on the road north. The ruins are free to visit and looked after by English Heritage.

title: Trafalgar House, Wiltshire (28 Days Later 2002)
description: The country mansion that Major West's soldiers hold as their blockade headquarters, five miles south of Salisbury. It is a PRIVATE HOUSE, hired out for weddings and events rather than open for tours.

title: Ennerdale Water, Cumbria (28 Days Later 2002)
description: The final act, with the cottage and the enormous cloth sign laid out for the passing jet, was shot around this Lake District lake. It is the quietest of the major lakes and has no road along its shore.

title: Shaun's flat, 83 Nelson Road (Shaun of the Dead 2004)
description: The Crouch End house Shaun shares with Pete and Ed, and the front garden where he steps over the fence. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE, so look from the pavement only.

title: Corner shop, 96 Weston Park (Shaun of the Dead 2004)
description: The shop Shaun walks to for a Cornetto while failing to notice the apocalypse. It was Weston Park Food in the film and now trades as a Londis convenience store.

title: The Winchester, 39 Monson Road (Shaun of the Dead 2004)
description: The Duke of Albany in New Cross Gate supplied the exterior of the Winchester Tavern, with interiors built at Ealing Studios. The pub closed and the building has been converted into flats.

title: Katie's house, 413 South McCadden Place (The Ring 2002)
description: The Hancock Park house where Katie admits she has already watched the tape, and where she dies in the closet. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE in Los Angeles, standing in for suburban Seattle.

title: Metropolitan State Hospital, Norwalk (The Ring 2002)
description: The psychiatric hospital where Rachel interviews the traumatised Becca. It is a working California state hospital and not open to visitors.

title: Hoose Library, Mudd Hall, USC (The Ring 2002)
description: Rachel's lighthouse research scene was shot in the philosophy library inside Mudd Hall on the USC campus. The cloistered brick building is one of the most filmed corners of the university.

title: Harbor Steps Apartments, Seattle (The Ring 2002)
description: Rachel and Aidan's apartment building on Western Avenue, at the top of the Harbor Steps above the waterfront. It is a private residential complex, though the public stairway beside it is open.

title: Photo shop, 1923 Fifth Avenue, Seattle (The Ring 2002)
description: The shop beneath the Seattle Monorail track where Rachel collects Katie's distorted photographs. The storefront has changed hands since filming.

title: Shelter Mountain Inn, Camp Firwood (The Ring 2002)
description: The cabins where the cursed tape is found were shot at Camp Firwood on the shore of Lake Whatcom near Bellingham. It operates as a Christian summer camp and is private property.

title: Deception Pass Bridge (The Ring 2002)
description: Rachel and Noah drive north over this 1935 steel arch bridge between Whidbey and Fidalgo islands on the way to the lighthouse. There is parking at either end and a walkway across.

title: Yaquina Head Lighthouse (The Ring 2002)
description: The Moesko Island Lighthouse of the film is Oregon's tallest lighthouse, north of Newport. It is still an active light, with tours run at the Yaquina Head Outstanding Natural Area.

title: Emerald Glen Farm, Monroe (The Ring 2002)
description: The Morgan horse ranch, where Rachel confronts Richard Morgan and finds the well, is a working farm on Yeager Road off Highway 2. It is PRIVATE PROPERTY.

title: Pacific Wilshire Bank, 18421 Ventura Boulevard (Drag Me to Hell 2009)
description: Christine refuses Mrs Ganush her loan extension inside what was then an empty bank building in Tarzana. The space has since been in use as a gym.

title: Cal State Northridge (Drag Me to Hell 2009)
description: Clay Dalton lectures in the psychology department, filmed on the CSUN campus in the San Fernando Valley. The campus is open to walk through.

title: Doheny Mansion, Chester Place (Drag Me to Hell 2009)
description: The medium's gothic house, where the seance goes very badly, is the 1899 Doheny Mansion on what is now the Mount St Mary's University Doheny campus. It opens for occasional booked tours rather than drop-in visits.

title: Christine's home, 1031 Everett Street (Drag Me to Hell 2009)
description: The hillside house above Everett Park where the Lamia torments Christine, also used in Training Day. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE.

title: Los Angeles Union Station (Drag Me to Hell 2009)
description: The station where Christine thinks she is leaving her curse behind and meets Clay on the platform. The 1939 concourse is open to the public.

title: Ashridge Estate, Hertfordshire (The Descent 2005)
description: The woodland approach to the cabin and the exterior scenes before the women go underground were shot in Ashridge Park. The estate woods are National Trust land with free access.

title: Pinewood Studios (The Descent 2005)
description: Every cave in the film is a set. Simon Bowles built the crawls, chambers and blood pool on stages here because shooting in a real cave was judged too dangerous. The studio is a working facility and closed to the public.

title: Palacio de Partarriu, Llanes (The Orphanage 2007)
description: This 19th century mansion outside Llanes in Asturias played the orphanage for four weeks of shooting before the production moved to sound stages in Barcelona. It is a PRIVATE HOUSE and appears on the town's cinema walking route, to be viewed from the road.

title: Casa Argelich, Rambla de Catalunya 34 (REC 2007)
description: The whole quarantined apartment block is this real Eixample building from 1896, including the entrance hall and the marble staircase. It has stood empty since 2004 and is used for film shoots, so there is nothing to visit inside.

title: Los Alamos High School (Let Me In 2010)
description: Owen's school, including the corridors and the bullying, was shot at the high school in Los Alamos. It is a working school in the town that built the atomic bomb.

title: Moana Apartments, Albuquerque (Let Me In 2010)
description: The courtyard apartment complex where Owen first meets Abby on the climbing frame, standing in for 1980s New Mexico suburbia. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENTIAL complex on Alvarado Drive.

title: Tom's Market, Vivian, Louisiana (The Mist 2007)
description: The supermarket exterior, where the mist rolls into the parking lot, was a grocery store on North Pine Street about 30 miles north of Shreveport. The building sat empty for years and was DEMOLISHED in 2023.

title: StageWorks of Louisiana, Shreveport (The Mist 2007)
description: The supermarket interior where most of the film takes place was a set built on a sound stage on Clyde Fant Parkway. It is a private production facility.

title: Emma and Henry's house, 3742 West 36th Avenue (Trick 'r Treat 2007)
description: The house where the jack-o'-lantern rule gets broken in the opening story, on a Vancouver street that supplied four of the film's homes. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE.

title: Wilkins house, 3707 West 36th Avenue (Trick 'r Treat 2007)
description: Principal Wilkins's house, complete with the garden he should not be digging in, one block of West 36th Avenue from the others. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE.

title: Rhonda's house, 3775 West 36th Avenue (Trick 'r Treat 2007)
description: Home of Rhonda, the girl the other kids take to the quarry, on the same Vancouver block as the rest of Warren Valley. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE.

title: Kreeg house, 3725 West 36th Avenue (Trick 'r Treat 2007)
description: The house where Mr Kreeg meets Sam in the final story, with the porch and the dog. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE.

title: Seodaejeon station, Daejeon (Train to Busan 2016)
description: The Daejeon Station sequence, where the passengers run into a platform full of infected soldiers, was shot at the quieter Seodaejeon station. It is a working commuter station.

title: Dongdaegu station, Daegu (Train to Busan 2016)
description: Platform and trackside scenes, including the hunt for a working locomotive after the line is blocked, were filmed at this major KTX station in Daegu. It is busy and open to travellers.

title: Cinespace Wilmington (The Black Phone 2021)
description: The Grabber's soundproofed basement, with the disconnected phone on the wall, was built on a stage at this Wilmington studio, formerly Carolco Studios. It is a working facility, not a tour.

title: Cape Fear Optimist Club fields (The Black Phone 2021)
description: The baseball diamond where Finney is introduced pitching, on North Kerr Avenue. The fields are still used for youth baseball.

title: Finney and Gwen's house, Pinecrest Parkway (The Black Phone 2021)
description: The home the siblings share with their father, and the street where Finney is snatched by the van. These are PRIVATE RESIDENCES in a lived-in Wilmington neighbourhood.

title: Acme-Delco Middle School (The Black Phone 2021)
description: The 1970s school the siblings attend, about 25 miles northwest of Wilmington on Andrew Jackson Highway. It is a working public school.

title: Sam Food Mart, Princess Place Drive (The Black Phone 2021)
description: The corner store that becomes Ellison's Grab'n'Go, where Robin buys sodas. It is still a neighbourhood convenience store.

title: The Grabber's house, 2415 Shirley Road (The Black Phone 2021)
description: The two houses facing each other at the end of the film, including the one with the black balloons. Both are PRIVATE RESIDENCES, and the big tree out front was added digitally.

title: St James Anglican Church, Vancouver (Heretic 2024)
description: The striking concrete church on East Cordova Street in the Downtown Eastside appears in the film, which otherwise shot mostly on stages at Pitt Meadows. It is a working parish church.

title: Brockett Elementary School, Tucker (Weapons 2025)
description: Maybrook Elementary, the school where seventeen children walk out of their beds at 2.17am, is this school on Brockett Road northeast of Atlanta. It is a working public school.

title: Alex's house, 4095 Brockett Creek Court (Weapons 2025)
description: Home of the one child who did not disappear, in a cul-de-sac that backs onto the school. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE.

title: USA Package, Conyers (Weapons 2025)
description: The liquor store Justine keeps returning to, on West Avenue in Conyers about 24 miles east of Atlanta. It is an operating store.

title: Trueco service station, Covington (Weapons 2025)
description: The gas station where Justine is confronted by a furious parent, a working BP on Pace Street in Covington. The forecourt is a public business, so keep out of the way.

title: Railroad Avenue, Donaldsonville (Sinners 2025)
description: The historic Railroad District was dressed as 1932 Clarksdale, Mississippi, with more than a dozen shopfronts, a cinema and a barber shop built for the shoot. The street itself remains a real Louisiana main street.

title: Creedmoor Plantation, St Bernard Parish (Sinners 2025)
description: Annie's home on Bayou Terre-aux-Boeufs, a raised house under old oaks east of New Orleans. It is PRIVATE PROPERTY and not open to visitors.

title: Hidden Oaks Golf Course, Braithwaite (Sinners 2025)
description: The sawmill and the juke joint were built from scratch on this overgrown course, which closed in 2006 after flooding from Hurricane Katrina. The site is private land southeast of New Orleans.

title: Laurel Valley Plantation, Thibodaux (Sinners 2025)
description: Field work and Jedidiah's church were shot at this former sugar plantation, where alfalfa stood in for cotton. The village of old quarters has a store and is open to visitors.

title: Church of St Mary and St Finnan, Glenfinnan (28 Years Later 2025)
description: The exterior of Jimmy's father's church, above Loch Shiel and a short walk from the Harry Potter viaduct. It is a working Catholic church.

title: St John the Baptist, Stanwick St John (28 Years Later 2025)
description: The interior of the church in the prologue, where the children hide as the infected come through the door, was shot in this isolated North Yorkshire church. It is usually open to visitors.

title: Holy Island of Lindisfarne (28 Years Later 2025)
description: The quarantined island community was filmed on Lindisfarne off the Northumberland coast. Check the tide tables before crossing, because the causeway floods twice a day.

title: Lindisfarne causeway (28 Years Later 2025)
description: The tidal crossing that keeps the survivors safe and traps them in equal measure. The road is submerged at high tide and people are rescued off it every year.

title: Jubilee Hall, Newton-on-the-Moor (28 Years Later 2025)
description: The village hall five miles south of Alnwick, with its barrel ceiling and wooden beams, played the island community's meeting place. It is still the local community hall.

title: Kielder Forest (28 Years Later 2025)
description: The woodland training and chase scenes were shot in England's largest planted forest, with its moss covered hills. There are waymarked trails and a visitor centre.

title: Kielder Water (28 Years Later 2025)
description: The reservoir and its dam works appear in the sequence where the Swedish soldiers are attacked. It is the largest artificial lake in northern Europe and ringed by a public path.

title: Sycamore Gap, Hadrian's Wall (28 Years Later 2025)
description: The dip in Hadrian's Wall beside Crag Lough, walked in the film's journey south. The famous tree that stood here was ILLEGALLY FELLED in September 2023, so only the stump and the wall remain.

title: Fountains Abbey, Ripon (28 Years Later 2025)
description: The travellers shelter overnight in these Cistercian ruins, founded in 1132. The abbey is a World Heritage Site run by the National Trust and is ticketed.

title: Embsay station, Embsay and Bolton Abbey Steam Railway (28 Years Later 2025)
description: The abandoned train is a heritage railway east of Skipton, which runs four miles of preserved line. It operates on public running days.

title: Cheddar Gorge, Somerset (28 Years Later 2025)
description: The limestone gorge in the Mendip Hills stands in for a solo stretch of the journey. The B3135 winds through it and the cliffs are open to walk.

title: Glenmaroon House, Knockmaroon Hill (Abigail 2024)
description: Almost all of the vampire ballerina film was shot inside this mansion on the edge of Phoenix Park, built for Guinness heir Arthur Ernest Guinness and later a convent and care home. The buildings are now vacant and PRIVATE, so view from the road.

title: Ardmore Studios, Bray (Abigail 2024)
description: Set work for the film was done at Ireland's oldest film studio in County Wicklow. It is a working studio and not open to the public.

title: Docklands Studios Melbourne (Late Night with the Devil 2023)
description: The entire 1977 talk show, Night Owls and its Halloween broadcast, was shot on Stage 5 here in about twenty days. The stage was already a television broadcast centre with audience seating, which is why it was chosen.

title: Villa Parisi, Monte Porzio Catone (Immaculate 2024)
description: Much of the convent was shot at this 1603 villa in the hills outside Rome, a veteran horror location used for A Bay of Blood, Blood for Dracula and Burial Ground. It is privately owned and hired for events and filming.

title: Galleria Doria Pamphilj, Rome (Immaculate 2024)
description: The gilded interiors of the order were filmed in this private palace gallery on Via del Corso. It is open as a ticketed art museum.

title: Studios d'Epinay, Epinay-sur-Seine (The Substance 2024)
description: Elisabeth's white tiled apartment, the bathroom and the New Year broadcast were all built on stages north of Paris. Nothing in the film was shot in Los Angeles despite the setting.

title: Elks Lodge 2190, Canoga Park (MaXXXine 2024)
description: The Landing Strip club, where Maxine dances early in the film, was shot in this fraternal lodge on Osborne Street. It is a private members club.

title: Maxine's apartment, 6410 Hollywood Boulevard (MaXXXine 2024)
description: Maxine's apartment building and the alley beside it, on the block of Hollywood Boulevard that was closed for four days of shooting. The ground floor is storefronts.

title: 6315 Hollywood Boulevard (MaXXXine 2024)
description: The strip club exterior and interior on the south side of Hollywood Boulevard, dressed back to grimy 1985. The block is now mostly tourist retail.

title: Hollywood Forever Cemetery (MaXXXine 2024)
description: Bodies are pulled from the pond in this cemetery on Santa Monica Boulevard, backing onto Paramount. It is open daily and hosts film screenings in summer.

title: Westin Bonaventure Hotel (MaXXXine 2024)
description: Maxine first meets the private investigator Labat in the revolving lounge at the top of this mirrored downtown hotel. The lobby and lounge are open to visitors.

title: Warner Bros Studios, Burbank (MaXXXine 2024)
description: The film opens on the lot here, with scenes shot outside Stage 15 and Stage 16 and at Gate 5. The studio runs paid tours.

title: Universal Studios backlot (MaXXXine 2024)
description: The chase and climax use the backlot's Western Street, Courthouse Square and the Psycho house and Bates Motel. The backlot is visible from the studio tram tour.

title: TCL Chinese Theatre (MaXXXine 2024)
description: Grauman's Chinese Theatre closes out Maxine's Hollywood story. The forecourt with the handprints is free to walk through.

title: Royal Whanganui Opera House (Pearl 2022)
description: Pearl's dance audition and her fantasy of the stage were shot in this 1899 opera house on St Hill Street. It is one of the few Victorian opera houses left in the southern hemisphere and still puts on shows.

title: Embassy 3 Cinema, Whanganui (Pearl 2022)
description: The picture house where Pearl escapes into the movies is on Victoria Avenue, which the production dressed back to 1918. It is still a working cinema.

title: Vincent Pier lighthouse, Scarborough (Saint Maud 2019)
description: The white lighthouse at the end of Vincent Pier in Scarborough's South Bay appears in Maud's wanderings. You can walk out to it around the harbour.

title: Foreshore Road, Scarborough (Saint Maud 2019)
description: The seafront strip of vintage amusement arcades and chip shops that gives the film its off-season seaside dread. It is busy in summer and eerie in February, which is the version the film uses.

title: Holbeck cliffs, Scarborough (Saint Maud 2019)
description: The crumbling cliffs at the south end of Scarborough, used for the film's exposed clifftop scenes. This is the slope that gave way in 1993 and took the Holbeck Hall Hotel with it.

title: St Michael and All Angels, Withington (Men 2022)
description: The church where Harper talks to the vicar and meets the naked man is in Withington, the Gloucestershire village that played the fictional Cotson. It is a working parish church about eight miles southeast of Cheltenham.

title: Bantry House, County Cork (Oddity 2024)
description: Damian McCarthy shot his West Cork horror at this Georgian stately home overlooking Bantry Bay. The house and gardens are open to visitors in season.

title: The blind man's house, 2488 W Buena Vista Street (Don't Breathe 2016)
description: The exterior of the house the three thieves break into, a 1924 home on a nearly empty Detroit block. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE, and every interior was built and shot at a studio in Hungary.

title: 8105 Mulholland Terrace (The Invitation 2015)
description: The entire dinner party plays out in this 1964 Hollywood Hills house, a few minutes from Cielo Drive. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE on a narrow hillside street.

title: Rosewood, 48 Haights Cross Road (Bodies Bodies Bodies 2022)
description: Nearly the whole film was shot in this Georgian stone manor in Chappaqua, which had sat unsold for years when the production took it over during Covid. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE and has since been bought.

title: The Oswalt house, 169 Middle Neck Road (Sinister 2012)
description: The house Ellison moves his family into, the one where the previous family was hanged in the yard. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE in Sands Point on Long Island.

title: 13236 Bavarian Drive, San Diego (Paranormal Activity 2007)
description: The whole film was shot in director Oren Peli's own house in Rancho Penasquitos over about seven days for roughly 15,000 dollars. It is a PRIVATE RESIDENCE, and the front of the house never appears on screen.

title: Durland Scout Reservation, Putnam Valley (Companion 2025)
description: The lakeside scenes were shot at this Scout camp on Clear Lake in Putnam County, because the house used for the film had no lake of its own. The water was extended digitally in post.

title: Auckland University of Technology city campus (M3GAN 2022)
description: The atrium of the toy company Funki, where Gemma builds her doll, is a university foyer on the AUT city campus. The campus is in central Auckland, and the city's suburbs were used elsewhere in the film to give it a Denver, Colorado feel.
